irregularities.title: Settled history in data/fe803b80/board.json cannot be used as a track record
irregularities.detail: The published track_record claims 99.5% accuracy for model-only picks (366 won / 2 lost) and 98.4% for market-only picks (121 / 2), while blended picks sit at 70.2%. Picks whose own published probability averages 0.667 cannot hit 99.5% of the time. Two mechanical causes are visible in the file: 'history' holds 4,870 rows for only 107 unique fixtures (the same fixture is re-recorded at every ~26-minute refresh, so samples are 20-200x inflated), and every 'settled: won' row has pick == winner by construction, which means the pick string is being re-derived from the result rather than from the published line. Anyone quoting 'our model hits 99%' from this file would be publishing a false claim.
irregularities.action: Not edited (file is another session's scope). Reported here and in COORDINATION.md; the day-5 desk republishes its own numbers from raw reads instead.

irregularities.title: Duplicate Valve VRS rows silently mis-joined
irregularities.detail: Valve's 2026_10_05 global file lists 'chinggis_warriors' twice (ranks 87 and 220) and 'betclic' twice (45 and 183) because retired lineups keep their rows. The board's vrs_ambiguous_keys contains only 'club333:americas:Club 333', and scripts/fe803b80/core.py has no ambiguity guard, so 1081863 was joined to a 685-point row when the active lineup holds 1084 points, and 1081546 could have been joined to the disbanded 765-point Betclic row. Both joins are corrected in this session's override file with the lineup evidence.
irregularities.action: Fix request logged for the board owner: refuse any rating join where the same team name matches more than one row unless the lineup also matches.

irregularities.title: bo3.gg shows one unlabeled number per finished match
irregularities.detail: The 'Odds' column on ended cards printed 3.80 for 9z v Aurora and 11.00 for Falcons v BETBOOM with no team attribution. Both cannot be the second team's price: HLTV's news for day 1 says Aurora were 'the only favorite to falter', which makes 3.80 the 9z price, while an 11.00 BETBOOM price would be consistent with HotSpawn's 'Huge underdogs' wording. Because the label is ambiguous we use the field for nothing.
irregularities.action: Excluded from the price set; documented so nobody re-adds it later.

irregularities.title: Rendered clocks are viewer-local on HLTV, the HotSpawn lobby and bo3.gg
irregularities.detail: Three independent traps in one hour: HLTV served the grand final as '11:00' to this session (a UTC-4 proxy) while its own search-indexed copy and Liquipedia show 17:00 CEST; the HotSpawn lobby rendered 'Oct 18, 04:00' next to a 'Locks in 07:06:12' countdown that only makes sense for an 08:00Z fixture; bo3.gg printed 'Oct 20, 03:00' for a fixture whose API epoch is 07:00Z. Any pick locked on a read of the printed clock would have been three to four hours late.
irregularities.action: Every time on this desk is UTC, decoded from HotSpawn's API epoch milliseconds; the rendered strings are only kept in the read ledger (R2, R11) as a consistency check on that decode.

irregularities.title: Auto-written 'insights' prose on bo3.gg contradicts the results page
irregularities.detail: The generator called the Aurora-Falcons third-place match 'the grand final' on two separate pages and credited Falcons with a 'two-match winning streak' the morning after they lost 1-2 to BETBOOM. Its FURIA '80% H2H winrate' line is a record count, not a probability.
irregularities.action: Only numeric tables (prices, map win rates, scores) are read from bo3.gg; its prose is never quoted as evidence and its AI 'projection' text is not a probability.

irregularities.title: The Day-2 desk in this repo published a price move that was not one, plus an unsupported 11.00
irregularities.detail: day2/picks.html (and two older copies) describe Aurora's move from 1.37 to 1.62 as 'shortening' and 'steaming moves' - a longer decimal is a price drifting AWAY from a team, so the stated edge was backwards - and the same pages cite 'BETBOOM 11.00 fav over Falcons 1.09' for day 4, a pair no source supports while HLTV's own analytics page for that match said Falcons were the bookmaker favorite.
irregularities.action: Day-5 prices were re-derived from raw reads only; no figure was inherited from the earlier desk pages. Older pages left in place (other sessions own them) and flagged here instead.

irregularities.title: Two different VRS snapshots are in play at this event
irregularities.detail: HLTV's event page states 'VRS date: Aug 3rd 2026' for the Thunderpick World Championship seeding, while the newest official file our model can read is 2026_10_05 - and HLTV's Aurora team page displays VRS #6 where the 5 Oct file has them #9. Event results after 5 Oct (e.g. 9z +62 pts to 1571, FURIA +23 for the semi win reported by skin.club) are in none of them.
irregularities.action: The model component always uses the newest official file and is capped at 15% weight, so a 13-day-old rating cannot override a live price. The lag is published on every rating-only row.

rejected_claims.claim: Aurora's roster change makes them underpriced for Day 5
rejected_claims.why: The rebuild finished 8 Jul 2026 and no October transfer is visible on the team page; 14 weeks and five events of games are priced in.

rejected_claims.claim: YEKINDAR is out of the grand final / FURIA are on a stand-in
rejected_claims.why: FURIA's five on HLTV's final page lists YEKINDAR, and he rated 1.39 in the 17 Oct semi; molodoy has been a settled starter, not a temporary sub.

rejected_claims.claim: 9z's 2-0 over Aurora proves dogs are value at this event
rejected_claims.why: 9z were the dogs and Aurora 'the only favorite to falter' - which is an argument that favorites are not safe at this LAN, not that 30% dogs are cheap. Our floor rule (no forced switch below 35%) exists for exactly this distinction.

rejected_claims.claim: HotSpawn's 100% Aurora / low FURIA ownership shows where the value is
rejected_claims.why: Both day-5 cards were at 1 pick each when this desk read them (00:32Z), single digits against a 20-pick floor. HotSpawn percentages are crowd behaviour, never a probability, and the climb rule needs 20+ picks before it says anything at all.
